_This page is generated from src/cli.ts and src/usage.ts, so it says what the tool does._

`skill-evals --help`, `skill-evals help`, `skill-evals help <command>` and `skill-evals <command> --help` print the help text on standard output and exit 0; `--help` wins over every other flag. A wrong command line prints the same commands and flags on standard error and exits 2.

## Commands

| Command                 | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `run`                   | Run every case against subject A and subject B, score both, and print a comparison.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `score`                 | Run every case against one subject and print its scores.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `calibrate`             | Run the subject against itself, five reps by default, and write noise.json beside results.json: how much each case score, check and the suite score move when nothing changed. run --noise reads it, so that a difference inside that spread reads "within noise".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `plan`                  | Print what run or score would make: the matrix of harnesses, cases, subjects and reps, the number of runs, and the cases that are not applicable. With --resume or --out naming an earlier command's directory, also an estimate of cost and duration. It starts no harness and writes nothing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `check`                 | Run one small prompt in each installed harness and show what its adapter reports.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `validate`              | Check a suite without running it: report every case that does not load and every skill name the subject lacks. Spends nothing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `rejudge <out dir>`     | Score the runs of an earlier command again, against the cases as they are now, without starting the agent. It reads the directory under its lock and never changes its results.json or results.jsonl: it writes results.rejudged.json beside them and prints the report, or the full set of files into --out. Judge answers come from the judge cache of the directory. A run whose prompt, files or setup changed is not re-scored; a run without a workspace archive (--keep-workspaces) keeps the old score of each check that needs files. |
| `diff <a> <b>`          | Compare two sets of results, each an output directory or a results.json: the score change of each case with its run counts, the checks that started or stopped failing, and the change in cost and duration. A warning block comes first when the models, harnesses, tool version or any case differ. It informs and exits 0; --strict turns a warning into exit 2.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `init <id>`             | Write prompt.md and case.json for a new case from a template of the given kind, under the cases directory. The id may be a path, such as routing/commit-guard. It refuses an id that no case could have and a directory that exists. Every template loads and passes validate; replace its placeholders before the first run.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `explain <id>`          | Print one case as a run reads it, as JSON in Markdown: the prompt, the layers of files in order, the setup steps, every check with its defaults written out, the capabilities it needs, and whether each installed harness can run it. A case with variants lists them. It starts no harness: what is installed comes from a lookup on PATH.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `show <out dir> <case>` | Print what one run did: one line for each transcript event, with its agent, kind, name and input or output cut at 200 characters, and then each check with its score and reason. A tool call is numbered as the checks number it (`call #0`), so a reason that quotes a call can be found. It reads the output directory of an earlier command, takes no lock, and changes nothing.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `list`                  | Show the harnesses in default-preference order, and the cases.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

## Flags

| Flag                           | Commands                                                                              | Default                                                                              | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--a <subject>`                | `run`, `plan`                                                                         | main                                                                                 | The baseline.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `--b <subject>`                | `run`, `plan`                                                                         | the project, uncommitted changes included                                            | The change.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--subject <subject>`          | `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`, `check`, `validate`, `show`                             | the project, uncommitted changes included; the first subject of the results for show | The subject to score, to probe, or to check the skill names of. For show, the label of a subject in the results.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--harness <ids\|all>`         | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`, `check`                                          | the first installed one; all for check                                               | Comma-separated harness ids.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--case <globs>`               | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`, `validate`, `rejudge`, `list`                    | every case                                                                           | Which case ids to run. A glob: * stays within one directory, ** crosses directories, ? is one character, {a,b} is either. Repeat the flag or separate globs with commas.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `--not-case <globs>`           | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`, `validate`, `list`                               | none                                                                                 | Case ids to leave out, as globs like those of --case.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `--tag <tags>`                 | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`, `validate`, `list`                               | no tag filter                                                                        | Run the cases that have any of these tags. Repeat the flag or separate tags with commas.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `--tag-all <tags>`             | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`, `validate`, `list`                               | no tag filter                                                                        | Run the cases that have all of these tags.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `--not-tag <tags>`             | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`, `validate`, `list`                               | none                                                                                 | Leave out the cases that have any of these tags.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--heldout`                    | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`, `validate`, `list`                               | off                                                                                  | Also run the held-out variants, the ones a case marks with heldout: true. Without it they are left out.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--targets`                    | `list`                                                                                | off                                                                                  | Print the coverage table: for each target skill, how many selected cases name it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `--cases <dir>`                | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`, `validate`, `rejudge`, `init`, `explain`, `list` | evals/cases in the project                                                           | The directory that holds the cases.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--reps <n>`                   | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`                                                   | 3                                                                                    | Runs for each subject and case.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--jobs <n>`                   | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`                                                   | 1                                                                                    | How many runs may be in flight at once. A positive integer. Each run has its own home, workspace and copy of the subject. results.json lists the records in plan order whatever order the runs end in; results.jsonl and the progress lines follow the order they end in.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `--retries <n>`                | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`                                                   | 0                                                                                    | Tries after the first for a run that failed for a reason that is not the agent's: a harness crash (a non-zero exit with no final event), a rate limit (the adapter says so), or a timeout before the harness produced any agent event (its opening init event does not count). A non-negative integer. A rate-limited run waits 30 seconds times its attempt number first. A setup failure, an isolation breach, any other invalid run and a low score are never retried. The run record's attempts lists the error, cost (null when none was reported) and duration of each earlier attempt. |
| `--max-cost <usd>`             | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`                                                   | no limit                                                                             | Stop starting runs once this command has spent this many US dollars, summing agent, judge and decision costs over the attempts it made; reused runs are not counted. A positive number. Runs in flight finish, with their judged and decision checks skipped, so they are invalid and --resume repeats them. The command exits 4. A usage error when a selected harness, the judge or a decision check reports no cost.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--max-duration <minutes>`     | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`                                                   | no limit                                                                             | Stop starting runs after this many minutes of wall time. A positive number; fractions are allowed. Runs in flight finish, with their judged and decision checks skipped. The command exits 4.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `--model <id>`                 | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`, `check`                                          | the harness's own default                                                            | Passed to the harness unchanged.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--min-score <0..1>`           | `run`, `score`, `plan`                                                                | no bar                                                                               | The lowest suite score that passes. The command exits 1 when the suite score of the subject (B for run) is lower.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `--min-delta <-1..1>`          | `run`, `plan`                                                                         | no bar                                                                               | The least score difference, B minus A, that the suite must show, on the suite delta and not on its interval. The command exits 1 when the delta is lower. A negative number lets B score lower by at most that much. A case's own minDelta is the same bar for that case. Only run compares two subjects: with score it is a usage error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `--noise <file>`               | `run`, `plan`                                                                         | none: the interval alone decides                                                     | A noise.json that calibrate wrote. A delta that is no larger than the noise it records for its case, or for the suite, reads "within noise", whatever its interval. A case that the file does not list is judged by its interval alone, and the report says so. A file of the wrong shape is a usage error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--seed <n>`                   | `run`, `calibrate`, `plan`                                                            | 1                                                                                    | The seed of the bootstrap behind every interval, a positive integer up to 4294967295. The same runs and the same seed give the same report, byte for byte. results.json records it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--max-invalid <fraction>`     | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`                                                   | 0: any invalid run exits 3                                                           | The share of the planned runs that may be invalid, from 0 to 1. The command exits 3 only when the invalid runs divided by the planned runs of the cases that apply are greater than this. A run that did not run because --max-cost or --max-duration stopped the command is not invalid.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `--report <formats>`           | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`                                                   | md                                                                                   | The report formats to write: md, json, junit or html. Repeat the flag or separate formats with commas. md goes to standard output, and only when it is listed. The others go to report.json, report.xml (JUnit) and report.html in the output directory. summary.json is always written there.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--judge-harness <id>`         | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`, `rejudge`                                        | the harness under test; the judge harness of the earlier command for rejudge         | The harness that scores judged checks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--judge-model <id>`           | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`, `rejudge`                                        | the value of --model; the judge model of the earlier command for rejudge             | The model that scores judged checks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `--judge-api <kind>`           | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`, `rejudge`                                        | a harness session; the judge path of the earlier command for rejudge                 | Ask the judge model over this API and start no harness process for it. Only anthropic. --judge-harness is then ignored.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--judge-url <url>`            | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`                                                   | the provider's own                                                                   | The base URL of the judge API.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--decision-model <id>`        | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`                                                   | none                                                                                 | The decision model that scores decision checks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--decision-url <url>`         | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`                                                   | the provider's own                                                                   | The base URL of the decision model's API.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `--decision-timeout <seconds>` | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`                                                   | 60                                                                                   | How long one request to the decision model may take. A positive integer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `--lenient`                    | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`, `validate`, `rejudge`, `explain`, `list`         | off: an unknown key is an error; what the earlier command used for rejudge           | Drop a key that a case file does not take, and warn, instead of failing. Keys that start with x- are always kept.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `--isolated`                   | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`                                                   | off: the harness loads what its settings say                                         | Start the harness with nothing loaded but the subject, and mark a run invalid when the harness reports anything else as loaded. Only harnesses that declare the isolated capability take it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--keep-workspaces`            | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`                                                   | off: no archive                                                                      | After a run's checks, archive its workspace, the seed it started from, its remote directory and its throwaway home as <run>.workspace.tar in the output directory, with the system tar. The harness's login files are left out of the home, and the grader's copy is never in it. results.json records each archive as workspaceArchive. rejudge reads the archive to score the checks that need files again. Needs tar on PATH.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--kind <kind>`                | `init`                                                                                | none: init needs it                                                                  | The kind of case init writes: trigger, negative, behaviour, pressure, agent, outcome or prose.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--rep <n>`                    | `show`                                                                                | 1                                                                                    | Which rep of the case show prints, counted from 1. A positive integer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--out <dir>`                  | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`, `check`, `rejudge`                               | a new temp directory; results.rejudged.json beside the earlier results for rejudge   | Where results go. A fresh run starts an empty results.jsonl there.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--resume <dir>`               | `run`, `score`, `calibrate`, `plan`                                                   | none: a fresh run                                                                    | Continue the earlier command whose output directory this is. It implies --out and must name the same directory as --out when both are given. A run whose key matches a valid record in results.jsonl is not repeated; every other run is made and added. It also turns the judge cache on.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `--strict`                     | `diff`                                                                                | off                                                                                  | Turn any warning at the top of the diff into exit code 2. Without it diff informs and exits 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--dry-run`                    | `run`, `score`                                                                        | off                                                                                  | Print what the command would run, as plan does, and exit 0. It starts no harness and writes nothing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

A subject is what a run loads: a directory, a git ref of the project, or `none`. [Subjects](../concepts/subjects.md) has the details. [Set a pass bar](../guides/pass-bars.md) explains `--min-score` and the exit codes, and [Decision checks](../guides/decision-checks.md) explains the decision model's flags.
